Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 60, verse 5:

﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾

This is the supplication of the believers, and at their head is our master Ibrahim: they say, "Our Lord, do not make us a trial [for those who disbelieve]..." [al-Mumtahanah]. How can a believer become a trial for the disbeliever? A believer becomes a trial for the disbeliever in two situations. If the believers are defeated in battle before the disbelievers, then the disbeliever is tried, because he will say: "If they were believers in God, they would not have been defeated," or "If they had a Lord who defends them, they would not have been defeated," or they say: "If they were truthful in their faith, they would not have been defeated," and this is a trial. Or the disbeliever is tried by the believer when he sees the people of faith committing sins and not adhering to God's method, so they become disinclined toward Islam and dislike being associated with it. This is the reality of the Muslims now: they repel people from the religion of God instead of drawing them to it. Therefore our scholars said: "The condition of this Ummah will not be set right except by that which set right its first generation."

The believer bears this responsibility, the responsibility of barring people from the religion of God. Therefore this supplication is: ﴿Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve.﴾ Make us ones who carry out Your commands in a way that makes others love the religion, and do not let us be an argument for them in turning away from Your religion.

This gives us the necessity of holding firmly to the teachings of the religion, so that no one looks at a Muslim or believer and says: "This is one who declares faith yet acts contrary to the teachings of his religion," and thus he becomes a cause of trial for others.
